title: Go for it now means the best price on offer beats break-even
summary: Between Punt (an edge under 1.5 points) and Check the news (5+), labels now come from the price. A pick is Go for it only when the best line and price across the sportsbooks gives it a chance at least a point above that price's break-even, and Lean otherwise, with the number to look for, like "worth a bet at +2 or better at -110." Before kickoff, the chance bar shows the chance at that best number, and its yellow line what that price needs, so a Go for it bar is always past the line.
why: Since cover chances were scaled to how often picks really win, every Go for it pick (a 3-5 point edge) showed 52% or less, below the 52.4% break-even marked on its own bar: the label said bet while the number said don't. The model's edge is worth about half a point to a point of line, and in the backtest each point of line was worth about 3% of hit rate, so the price you get decides whether a pick is worth it.
effect: Far fewer Go for it picks: this week 4 of 30 labeled spread picks instead of 15, and no total. Most of them get there through a better price or number at one book, which the site can't name, so check your own book against the number. Quotes more than 1.5 points from the middle of the books are now ignored as feed errors. Alerts call new picks New pick and give the number to look for, since they can't follow prices after they're sent.
forward_test: Unchanged: the pick log records edges, not labels.

title: Easier on phones: keeps your place, today's games first, lighter logos
summary: Going back from a game now returns you to the same spot in the list, and every tab keeps its own place; tap the tab you're on to jump to the top. Games still to play come first, and finished games fold into a Final section at the bottom, latest first. Team logos load at the size they're shown, which cuts a week's worth from about 5.5 MB to 0.4 MB, and the dark theme uses ESPN's dark-mode logos, so navy and black ones stay visible. Tables on game pages and the Track record's recent picks rearrange to fit a phone instead of hiding columns off the edge; tables that still need a swipe fade at the edge and keep the first column in view. The How to read a game card guide moved from the bottom of the list to a ? button next to the team search.

title: Line shopping: the best number across sportsbooks
summary: Pick boxes now say when a better spread or total than the one shown is available at another US sportsbook, and each game page has a Line shopping table with the best number for each side, the middle number and how many books were quoted. The numbers come from The Odds API and are checked every 30 minutes on Sundays, when lines open, and every 8 hours otherwise. Sportsbooks aren't named, and quotes priced worse than -125 are left out. Half a point is worth about as much as the model's whole edge, so it pays to look. Each change is also saved with its time, building a record of lines that could really be bet.

title: Cover chances now match how often picks really win, and QB changes no longer change labels
summary: The chance shown for a pick used to read the model's whole disagreement with the line at face value. It now believes only the share of that gap that history supports (about a fifth for Blend), so most picks show 50-55%. Separately, a QB change tag no longer turns a pick into Check the news; it stays on the card for context. Picks on a team whose starting quarterback is listed out on an official report are still labeled Check the news.
why: Blend gaps of 10+ points showed about an 80% chance to cover and won 47-59% in 2024-2026, and no range of edge sizes reliably beat another. The QB change label was based on 57 games from 2026, where picks went 39%. With box scores for 2023-2026, Blend's picks in those games went 54% at the opening line against 57% in the rest, and 53% against 53% at the closing line. The 2026 result was a small-sample fluke, and the flag covered almost a quarter of all games.
effect: The percentages are smaller and honest: a 5-point Blend edge shows about 52.5%, right at the 52.4% break-even. Projections, edges and the labels by edge size don't change, so the labels say how much the model disagrees with the line, not how likely a pick is to win. More games show Lean or Go for it, because QB change games keep their label.
forward_test: The pick log is unchanged; it records edges, not chances.

title: Blend is now the default projection, with a new Success rate rating
summary: Spread picks now default to Blend, which averages ESPN FPI, Efficiency and a new Success rate rating (the share of plays each offense wins, adjusted for opponents). Market-anchored is still on the list but no longer the default. Lines are now checked every 30 minutes on Sunday afternoons and evenings, when most of them open, and the Track record tab leads with closing-line results. If you never chose a projection, yours switched to Blend; choosing another one sticks.
why: Market-anchored was the weakest projection in testing: 51.1% on 1.5+ edges at the opening line in 2024-2026, and 47% this season, against 55.9% for the new Blend. Its formula leans on the line so heavily that its edges came from a built-in lean, not from the ratings. Its live record on 1.5+ edges was 17-30. Testing also showed that lines move about a point toward the model's picks, and most of that happens within hours of the open, before the site first saw them.
effect: Blend disagrees with the line by 1.5+ points in about 70% of games, so expect many more labeled picks, and bigger edges did no better than smaller ones. Honest expectations: about 52% at lines you can get late in the week, up to 55% at true opening numbers. Elo, last season's SP+, talent ratings and explosiveness were tested too and didn't help. Totals still use Market-anchored.
forward_test: Nothing already logged changes. Every projection keeps its own rows in the pick log; Blend picks logged before this date averaged two ratings instead of three. Alerts and the Recent picks table now follow Blend.

title: Starting quarterbacks listed out on the official reports now mean Check the news
summary: When a team's usual starting quarterback is listed out or doubtful on an official availability report, picks on that team are labeled Check the news, the game card gets a QB tag, the game page shows the listing, and an alert goes out. The reports come from the Power 4 conferences for conference games and are entered by hand, because they're published through an app with no public data feed. Game pages also link to each conference's reports.
why: Box scores from 2023-2026 show that a team whose starting quarterback sat after playing the week before covered 43% at the opening line (317 games), and Market-anchored's picks on such a team went 16-20. By the second game the market and the ratings have caught up (51%), and missing running backs or receivers showed no effect at all, so they aren't flagged.
effect: Labels only. Projections and edges don't change, and picks against the team keep their label: they went 29-18. Only Power 4 conference games are covered (39% of these cases in 2023-2025), and some of the 317 were benchings rather than injuries. The ±1.6-point range on the effect only just excludes zero.
forward_test: The pick log is unchanged. Each listing is logged with the time it was first seen, so the forward test can check these games before any points adjustment is considered.

title: Market-anchored totals now follow the ratings instead of leaning over
summary: The Market-anchored total now moves the betting total a fifth of the way toward the Adjusted points total: total + 0.2 x (ratings total - total). The ratings have to disagree with the market by 7.5 points for a Lean and 15 for a Go for it, so it flags about 7 games a week instead of 15, and it always picks the same side as Adjusted points.
why: The old formula was fit to the average final score, which a few shootouts pull up, so it learned that low totals go over and barely used the ratings. 96% of its 1.5+ edges were overs, and in 2026 they went 56-55. Week 9 went under and it went 19-33. When the ratings disagreed with the opening total by 5+ points, siding with them won in every season from 2022 to 2026 (53.7%, and 56.2% at 7+), on overs and unders alike.
effect: In 2024-2026, 1.5+ edges at the opening total went 56.2% (131-102) instead of 53.8%, with 64% overs instead of 96%. At the closing total it's 52.5%, so getting the opening number matters. The 0.2 was chosen after looking at these seasons, so treat the backtest as a little flattering. Spreads don't change.
forward_test: Totals picks already logged (week 9 and the week 10 games logged so far) keep the old formula; new totals are logged with the new one, and the logged_at time shows which.

title: Check the news for quarterback changes, bowl games and windy overs
summary: Three situations the ratings can't see now turn a Lean or Go for it into Check the news, with the reason in the pick box. A QB change tag marks games where a team's usual starter didn't lead its last game in pass attempts (from ESPN box scores). Bowl games outside the College Football Playoff are labeled the same way. On totals, an over pick with 12+ mph of wind in the kickoff forecast is too, and a Wind tag shows the forecast. Game pages get a Quarterbacks and injuries card and the forecast on the over/under card.
why: In 2026, the model's picks went 39% at the opening line in games right after a quarterback change (57 games), against 55% in the rest. In 2023-2025 bowls outside the playoff, FPI went 42% and Blend 47% (109 games), while playoff games went 60-68%. In windy games, totals fell about 1.8 points between the open and kickoff and overs went 48% against the opening total. In each case the market knows something the ratings don't.
effect: Labels only. Projections, edges and cover chances don't change, and the Go for it filter and counts leave these games out. The quarterback and bowl samples are small.
forward_test: The pick log is unchanged: picks are still logged with their edge size, so the forward test can show whether these games really do worse.

title: Ready for bowl season and the offseason
summary: Bowl and playoff results now count toward the ratings and the QB watch, game cards show the bowl, playoff or conference championship name, and alerts label non-playoff bowls Check the news. A replay of the 2025 postseason through the whole pick log (46 games) caught a bug that would have logged every playoff game twice; that's fixed. After the national championship, the Games tab says the season is over instead of showing an empty week, and on July 1 the site switches to the new season, rating every team by ESPN's preseason FPI until games are played.

title: Efficiency (EPA per play) added, and Blend now uses it
summary: A fifth projection, Efficiency, rates every offense and defense by expected points added (EPA) per play, adjusted for opponents and with garbage time left out, from CollegeFootballData. Blend now averages FPI and Efficiency instead of FPI and adjusted points. The Ratings tab shows each team's offensive and defensive EPA. Market-anchored, the default, is unchanged.
why: Points are a noisy measure of how good a team is: a pick-six or a garbage-time touchdown counts the same as a long drive. EPA per play measures every snap.
effect: Small. On the same 2024-2026 games, the new Blend went 54.4% at the opening line on every game (old Blend 53.3%) and 52.2% at the closing line (old 50.1%), with the same accuracy; on 3+ point edges the two were even. It wasn't better in every season (2025 dipped), and in 2022, a season nothing was tuned on, Efficiency alone did only 51.7% at the opening line on 3+ edges. Starting each season from last year's efficiency, and adding it to Market-anchored, were also tested and didn't help.
forward_test: Efficiency picks are logged from October 29, 2026. Blend picks logged before then used adjusted points and aren't changed, so Blend's forward-test record mixes the two until the old picks age out.

title: Alerts: new edges and key-number line moves
summary: A bell at the top of the site opens Alerts. You get one when the model finds an edge of 1.5+ as soon as a line opens, or when a line moves through, onto or off 3 or 7 on a game it has a pick for. Follow them in any RSS reader with the feed address in the panel, which also lists the latest alerts. Phone notifications (through the free ntfy app) and a Discord channel can be switched on by the site's owner. Checked every two hours, with at most one notification per check.

title: Over/unders: a totals pick for every game
summary: A new Spread / Total switch on the Games tab shows the model's over/under pick for every game, from two new totals projections: Market-anchored (the default) starts from the betting total and adjusts it slightly toward what the teams' scoring says, and Adjusted points adds each offense's points against the other's defense. Game details get an Over/under card, and you can track total picks in My picks.
why: Totals are part of every game, and the only way to know whether the model can pick them is to record its picks before kickoff, the same way spreads are recorded.
effect: Spread picks don't change. In the 2023-2026 backtest, totals came out about break-even: 52.1% at the opening total for Adjusted points (2,272 picks), and 51-52% at the closing total. They're shown as untested, not as a proven edge. The model doesn't know the weather, which matters more for totals.
forward_test: Over/under picks are logged in a separate file, data/live/total_picks.csv, from October 29, 2026. The spread pick log is untouched. This week's games are logged at their current total, not their opening one.

title: Track record leads with line movement, and shows margins of error
summary: The forward test now leads with an expected hit rate estimated from how far lines moved toward the picks, with its margin of error, a bar showing where it sits against the 52.4% break-even, and a plain verdict. A win-loss record needs hundreds of picks to mean much (after 50 its margin of error is about ±14 points), while line moves say more much sooner: in the 2023-2026 backtest, each point the line moved toward a pick was worth about 3 points of hit rate. Every hit rate on the tab now shows its ± margin of error, and a Spreads / Totals switch covers both.

title: At open: edges still at the opening number
summary: The model tested best against opening lines, so a new At open filter shows edges of 1.5+ where the line hasn't moved more than half a point since it opened. Pregame pick boxes say how far the line has moved toward or away from the pick. When next week's lines post (usually Sunday), a notice at the top of the Games tab says how many edges are still at the opening number and links straight to them.

title: Player props: projections for this week's players
summary: A new Props tab projects passing yards, passing TDs, rushing yards, receiving yards and receptions for players in this week's games, from ESPN box scores. Enter the line and odds from your sportsbook to see the chance of going over or under, how often the player cleared that line in his last five games, and a lean when the chance beats the odds' break-even by 3+ points. The projections are a season average, nudged for the opponent's defense on rushing yards, passing TDs and receptions; weighting recent games more tested worse. They've never been tested against real prop lines, since free historical prop lines don't exist, and the tab says so.

title: 5+ point edges now say Check the news, and Market-anchored was retrained
summary: Edges of 5 or more points are no longer labeled Go for it. They show a caution badge, Check the news, instead. Go for it now means a 3-5 point edge. Market-anchored was also retrained on the corrected backtest data.
why: Once look-ahead opening lines were removed (see the correction below), 5+ point edges did no better than 3-5 point ones: ESPN FPI's went 52.6% at the opening line and about 50% at the closing line. A gap that big usually means the market knows something the model can't see, like an injury or a quarterback change.
effect: Market-anchored now leans more on the betting line (weight 0.57 to 0.73) and less on FPI (0.39 to 0.21), so it shows big edges much less often. The bad lines had made FPI look more useful than it is.
forward_test: Picks already logged keep their original numbers. New picks use the retrained Market-anchored weights. The forward-test summary still groups every 3+ point edge together.

title: Correction: the backtest's opening-line results were too optimistic
summary: About 3% of the historical opening lines (63 of 2,323 games) were look-ahead lines posted weeks before kickoff. Those lines then moved 7+ points by game time, as when Oklahoma vs Texas in 2023 opened Oklahoma +6.5 and closed -5.5. Nobody could have bet them with that season's information, but they made the model's biggest edges look like big winners. They're now excluded. At the opening line, ESPN FPI's 3+ point edges went from 55.7% to 53.8%, and Market-anchored's from 60.5% (172 picks) to 62.1% on just 29 picks. Closing-line results barely changed and stay around 50%. The edge at the opening line is real but small, barely above the 52.4% needed to break even.

title: Close filter: live games near the spread
summary: A new Close button next to Live shows games in progress where the score is within 4 points of the spread, so a field goal could flip who covers. They're sorted tightest first, and every close game gets a yellow tag on its card, like "Close · 2.5 from the spread", under any filter.

title: Ratings tab explains itself, plus a matchup tool
summary: A How to read the ratings guide covers what every column means, how each projection turns the ratings into a predicted margin, a worked example with today's numbers, and tips. A new Compare two teams tool shows what each projection predicts for any matchup, home or neutral, and if you enter the betting line, which side it would pick and how big the edge is. Hover a column name for a quick definition.

title: Clearer picks and results on every game
summary: From user feedback: each game now has a labeled Model pick box with the team's logo and line, and the picked team gets a PICK tag next to its score. Finished games say plainly whether the pick covered (a green ✓ Covered or red ✗ Missed) with a sentence like "Delaware won by 23, covering −3 by 20 points." Live games show Covering now or Not covering yet, and game details use the same box.

title: Updates tab and a way to send suggestions
summary: This page: every improvement in one place, newest first. You can also suggest a change or report something that looks wrong, which opens a pre-filled issue on GitHub so it's tracked in the open.

title: Home-field advantage raised from 2.5 to 3.0 points
summary: The home team now gets 3 points instead of 2.5 in every projection, and Market-anchored was retrained to match.
why: Week 8's picks leaned heavily toward road teams, and home teams went 23-14 against the spread. A check of 2023-2026 found the projections underrated home teams slightly at 2.5 points; at 3.0 that bias goes away.
effect: Small. In the 2023-2026 backtest, ESPN FPI's picks at the opening line went from 53.3% to 54.0%, and every projection moved by less than one percentage point. Market-anchored was retrained and barely changed.
forward_test: Picks already in the forward-test log were made with 2.5 and are not changed. Picks logged from October 25, 2026 on use 3.0.

title: Game details keep live scores fresh
summary: A game's detail page now updates its score and clock every 30 seconds from ESPN's latest data, starts updating 15 minutes before kickoff if you opened it early, and shows when it last updated.

title: Cleaner Games toolbar
summary: Filters became one segmented control with game counts built in, plus a search box and matching dropdowns. Every button group on the site now shares the same style, and nothing gets cut off on small phones.

title: Game details: tap any game for the full breakdown
summary: What all four projections say and whether they agree, how the line moved through the week, the matchup, ESPN's win chance, weather, the forward-test entry, and a live win-chance chart during the game. Each game has its own shareable link.

title: New name: Fourth & Value
summary: The project was renamed from CFB Edge, with a new broadcast-football look and edge labels that read like fourth-down calls: Go for it, Lean and Punt. The site moved to davischamann-alt.github.io/fourth-and-value; the old address no longer works.

title: Cleaner pick-log history
summary: The two-hourly recording job now saves to GitHub only when a line moves, a new game is logged, or a result comes in, so every entry in the log's history means something happened.

title: Tried and removed: run your own backtest
summary: A panel for running backtests in the browser with your own CollegeFootballData key was added and then taken out the same day. It may come back later.

title: Market-anchored starts from the line you'd actually bet
summary: Market-anchored used to start from the opening line even after the line had moved. It now starts from the current line, or the pregame line once a game has started.
why: Starting from an old line counted the line's own movement as edge. Texas A&M at Alabama opened at Alabama -2.5 and moved to -14, which showed a 5.4-point 'Go for it' edge that was really just the line move. The backtest always started from the same line it graded against, so this matches how the model was tested.
effect: Fewer, more honest edges: that week's strong edges dropped from 10 to 4. Backtest results don't change.
forward_test: Made before the first forward-test pick was logged, so every logged pick uses it.

title: Forward test: every pick recorded before kickoff
summary: Every two hours, each game's picks are saved the first time its line appears and never changed afterward, then graded when the game ends. The history on GitHub proves when each pick was made. Results are on the Track record tab.

title: The website launches
summary: A free, no-install site that works on phones: live game cards with cover chances, ratings, tracked picks, a bet tracker and the track record. Ratings refresh automatically every morning.

title: Market-anchored projection added
summary: A new projection that starts from the betting line and shifts it toward what ESPN FPI and adjusted points say, with weights learned from past seasons.
why: The plain projections predicted margins from scratch, and the market beat them. Starting from the line and adjusting only where the ratings disagree tested better.
effect: Fewer picks, but its 3+ point edges hit about 60% at the opening line in the 2024-2026 backtest (a small sample).

title: Backtest covers past seasons and opening lines
summary: Picks are now tested on 2021-2026 using CollegeFootballData, graded against both opening and closing lines, with closing line value: how often the line moved toward each pick.

title: Opponent-adjusted ratings and ESPN FPI
summary: Ratings went from raw points per game to points adjusted for opponent strength, and ESPN's Football Power Index was added as a second projection.
why: Raw scoring averages missed the market's line by about 8.8 points per game; opponent adjustment cut that to 3.3, and FPI to 2.3.
effect: Projections land much closer to the betting line, so far fewer false edges.

title: First version
summary: A dashboard on one computer comparing a simple scoring model to the Vegas spread, with live cover chances, a bet tracker and pick logging.
